name: Isosorbide dinitrate

sources.citation: Bausch Health US LLC. Isordil Titradose (isosorbide dinitrate) tablets. DailyMed set 8ddd2577-311a-4967-bb67-ad72e2b76f83; verified 25 November 2026. Oral immediate-release US reference, not IV or sublingual instructions.

revision_log.change: Faithful US-label summary with formulation-specific doses and kidney limitations; no inferred regimen or personal physician-review claim.
revision_log.approved_by: Codex source verification under the existing delegated workflow.

overview.mechanism: Relaxes vascular smooth muscle, especially veins [[ISDN]].
uses: The oral Isordil Titradose label covers angina prevention, not acute-attack termination [[ISDN]].

usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 5–20 mg two or three times daily; maintenance 10–40 mg two or three times daily, with at least a 14-hour daily dose-free interval [[ISDN]].

dose_note: Oral immediate-release reference only. Sublingual, sustained-release and IV products require separate instructions. Dinitrate and mononitrate are not interchangeable dosing headings [[ISDN]].
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; concomitant PDE5 inhibitors or riociguat [[ISDN]].

serious: Severe hypotension, sometimes with bradycardia or increased angina [[ISDN]].

monitoring: Blood pressure, orthostatic symptoms, volume depletion and dose-free interval adherence [[ISDN]].

key_interactions.effect: Severe hypotension, syncope or myocardial ischemia [[ISDN]].

renal: No kidney-adjustment or dialysis schedule is inferred from the cited oral label. Avoid interpreting absent instructions as proof of safety in kidney failure [[ISDN]].

rows.intervention: Scheduled treatment with a daily drug-free interval.
rows.findings: Continuous exposure causes tolerance; later daily doses can have smaller, shorter effects.
rows.limitations: Not an IV or sublingual regimen; oral treatment cannot abort an acute attack.
